findings.finding: Installed schema permits function_call_output without a nonempty call ID. Global identity validation rejects such an item, including outside the chosen interval. Root retained fail-closed missing/ambiguous identity and unresolved/overlap behavior for this bounded method; the review does not propose relaxing those gates.

Direct exec completed output is formatted text: optional Chunk ID line, Wall time: decimal seconds, Process exited with code 0, optional Original token count line, then Output: and a newline followed by payload. EXEC_HEADER agrees with this format. Direct raw output is not the nested code-mode result JSON object.

Code-mode prepared output has Script completed, Wall time decimal seconds with optional code-mode/overhead timing, then Output and newline. Text content is a string or ordered input_text items. Whole-object exec printing uses chunk_id, wall_time_seconds, exit_code, session_id, original_token_count and output; optional absent fields are omitted. The reader consumes the complete supported body, rejects unfinished sessions and nontext/unknown envelopes, and requires exact executor-stdout equality.

Retained native source records the raw call before scheduling its tool future and emits prepared response items from the recording path. This supports call-before-command-before-output interval reasoning. The source tag and installed version label do not attest the exact installed executable build.

findings.finding: emittedAtMs is an integer Unix-millisecond timestamp. Reviewed helper requires strict raw-call time before command completion and bounds submillisecond executor request time by raw event times. Existing literal execution_proof similarly requires capture-close delivery no later than the app completion timestamp divided by 1000. Same-millisecond fast operations may be rejected conservatively even when event order is correct. No empirical occurrence or false-positive admission is claimed; the existing behavior remains unchanged in the narrow unrelated-output fix.
